title: Bhishma's fall
hook: kings run up with soft pillows for the fallen grandsire, and he sends every one of them away
carry: a plea for peace that Duryodhana turned down

segments.voice: Yesterday Bhishma fell: he knew Arjuna's arrows as they struck, and both armies stood still around the bed of arrows. Today, the last scene of this stretch.

His body is held up by arrows, but his head isn't. It hangs down, unsupported. Bhishma asks for something to rest it on. And the kings around him do the obvious thing. They run to their tents and come back with pillows, soft ones, fine ones, the best in the camp. Bhishma turns them all away. These don't belong on a bed like this one, he says, in effect. Then he looks at Arjuna. Today, what a grandson brings instead of a pillow, and the last thing Bhishma asks of the war.
screen: `HIS HEAD HANGS DOWN.` → `SOFT PILLOWS.` → `HE SENDS THEM AWAY.`

segments.voice: Bhishma asks Arjuna for a pillow fit for a hero's bed, and Arjuna understands. With tears in his eyes, the text says, he takes up his bow and drives arrows into the ground beneath Bhishma's head, so the head rests on them. A warrior's pillow for a warrior's bed. Bhishma is pleased. It's the same grandson whose arrows brought him down, and now his arrows are the only thing Bhishma will let hold him. Later Bhishma is thirsty. Again they bring the camp's best, cool water in fine vessels, and again he declines. He turns to Arjuna, who shoots an arrow into the earth beside him, and a stream of pure, cool water springs up, and Bhishma drinks. Then the old man uses what strength he has left for one more piece of counsel, this time to Duryodhana. You've seen what Arjuna can do, he says, in Ganguli's telling. Let the war end with me. Make peace with your cousins, give them their share, and let everyone go home. Duryodhana hears it, and he doesn't take it. The war will go on. So that's Bhishma's fall: an honest answer in his own tent, an old wrong from Amba's life, arrows he recognized, a bed held above the earth, and a grandson who knew exactly what kind of pillow to bring. And one last plea for peace that nobody accepted.
screen: `A PILLOW OF ARROWS` · `WATER FROM THE EARTH` · `"LET THE WAR END WITH ME"` · then, large: `DURYODHANA REFUSES`

segments.voice: Let your head find its own balance, chin slightly down, neck easy. Bring to mind someone who once gave you exactly what you needed, not what was easiest to give, and breathe in what they brought, breathe out a little thanks, even if things between you are tangled. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayer.
Bhishma's fall. It ends with a pillow of arrows, water drawn from the ground, and a plea for peace that went unheard.
Your line: a plea for peace that Duryodhana turned down. Tomorrow a new commander rides out: Drona. See you then.

howItsDone: Some paintings and temple carvings show Bhishma on the bed of arrows with his head resting on Arjuna's arrows, and storytellers return to the pillow and the spring of water when they tell his fall.

drive arrows into the ground to hold his head.
send for his own pillow from Hastinapura.
fork.reveal: Arjuna drives arrows into the ground beneath his head, a warrior's pillow, and Bhishma is pleased.

original.note: grandsire: the title the Pandavas and Kauravas use for Bhishma.

trapdoor: what you thought: Arjuna gave Bhishma a strange pillow.
what it means: he gave the pillow that fit a warrior's bed, the one Bhishma wanted.
what a scholar hears: the arrows that killed him now hold him, and the same hands that brought him down now care for him.

chat.says: Why did Bhishma turn down the soft pillows they brought him?
options: They didn't fit a warrior's bed; he wanted Arjuna's arrows to hold his head.
He was too proud to accept anything at all from the Kaurava camp.
He said soft pillows would lull him to sleep before his chosen hour.
chat.meaning: Bhishma asked for a pillow fit for a hero's bed. Arjuna, in tears, drove arrows into the ground to hold his head, and Bhishma was pleased.

Arjuna.meaning: the grandson whose arrows brought Bhishma down, and then held him

Duryodhana.meaning: the Kaurava prince who turns down Bhishma's plea for peace

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva (Bhishma-vadha Parva), the pillow of arrows, the water from the earth and Bhishma's counsel to Duryodhana

notes: All paraphrase. The number of arrows for the pillow is left out on purpose; confirm Arjuna's tears and Bhishma's pleasure in Ganguli.
Confirm the water scene: Bhishma refuses the brought water, Arjuna pierces the earth, and the text's description of the stream (some tellings link it to Ganga; left out here).
Confirm Bhishma's plea to Duryodhana to make peace and Duryodhana's refusal; the quoted-looking line is paraphrase, not Ganguli's wording.
